title: Advanced Reported Speech
description: Master advanced reported speech for Grade 12: a wide range of reporting verbs and their patterns (verb + gerund / infinitive / that-clause), and reporting full passages — bilingual notes and tests.

topics.title: Reporting Verbs & Their Patterns
topics.concept:
Advanced narration replaces 'said' with a verb that names the speech act. Each verb has a fixed pattern:

Reporting verbPatternExample
admit / deny+ gerundadmitted stealing / denied stealing
suggest / recommend+ gerund or that + (subjunctive)suggested going / suggested that we go
promise / agree / refuse / offer / threaten+ to-infinitivepromised to come; refused to pay
advise / warn / remind / urge / order+ object + to-infinitiveadvised me to rest; warned her not to drive
insist / complain / claim / boast+ that-clauseinsisted that he was innocent
apologise (for) / accuse (of) / congratulate (on)+ preposition + gerundapologised for being late

Choose the verb that matches the speaker's intention, then apply its pattern exactly.

examples.problem: Report precisely: "I didn't break the vase," she said.
Report precisely: "You should see a doctor," he said to me.
examples.solution: He advised me to see a doctor. — 'advise' + object + to-infinitive.

recap: insist/claim/complain + that-clause; apologise for / accuse of + gerund

topics.title: Reporting a Passage (Mixed Dialogue & Narrative)
topics.concept:
To report a whole passage, work through it utterance by utterance, asking: what is the speaker doing? (stating, asking, advising, refusing, apologising…). Then:

  1. Choose the most precise reporting verb for that act.
  2. Apply its pattern (gerund / infinitive / that-clause).
  3. Apply the usual changes — tense back-shift, pronouns, and time/place words.
  4. Link the reports smoothly with conjunctions ('and', 'but', 'then', 'finally').

Example passage:
Direct: "I'm sorry I'm late," said Ravi. "I won't be late again, I promise. Shall we begin?"
Reported: Ravi apologised for being late and promised not to be late again. He then suggested beginning / asked whether they should begin.

examples.problem: Report: "Don't touch the wires," the engineer warned us.
examples.solution: The engineer warned us not to touch the wires.

examples.problem: Report: "Yes, I took the last biscuit," he said.

recap: Identify each speech act, then pick the precise reporting verb
Apply its pattern + the usual back-shift/pronoun/time changes
Link the reports smoothly into one flowing paragraph

questions.q: 'admit' is followed by:
Report: '"I won't do it," he said.'
Report: '"You should rest," the doctor told her.'
options: The doctor advised her to rest.

questions.q: 'suggest' takes:
Report: '"I'll be there at five," she said.'
options: She promised being there at five.
She promised to be there at five.

questions.q: Report: '"Don't park here," the guard told us.'
options: The guard warned us not to park there.
The guard warned us to not parking.
The guard warned to not park.
The guard warned that park not.

questions.q: 'accuse' combines with:
Report: '"Sorry I shouted," he said.'
Report: '"Let's go for a walk," she said.'
options: She suggested going for a walk.
She suggested to go for a walk.

questions.q: 'remind' takes:
Report: '"I really did clean my room," he said.'
options: He insisted that he had cleaned his room.

questions.q: Report: '"Shall I carry that?" he said.'
Report the passage line: '"I'm warning you — leave now, or there'll be trouble," he said.'
options: He warned me to leave at once, threatening trouble otherwise.
He warned me leaving at once.
He warned to leave or trouble.
questions.explanation: 'warn + object + to-inf', with 'threatening' capturing the second clause.

questions.q: Choose the correct report: '"It was entirely my fault," she confessed.'
options: She confessed that it had been entirely her fault.
She confessed to be her fault.
She confessed her fault to be.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'He suggested me to take a break.'
options: suggested me to take → suggested (that I) take / suggested taking
questions.explanation: 'suggest' does not take 'object + to-infinitive'; use a gerund or that-clause.

questions.q: Report: '"You can rely on me to finish on time," she assured him.'
options: She assured him that she would finish on time.
She assured him to finish on time.

questions.q: Which report best captures '"No, no — I really must insist on paying," he said.'
Report: '"I'm thinking of resigning," he admitted.'
options: He admitted to think of resigning.

questions.q: Rearrange into a precise report: 'cheating / of / accused / the / examiner / him'
options: The examiner accused him of cheating.
The examiner accused him to cheat.
The examiner accused cheating him of.
Him the examiner accused of cheat.

questions.q: Choose the best single-verb report: '"Don't forget to lock up," she said to me.'
options: She reminded me to lock up.

outcomes: Use a wide range of reporting verbs precisely
Match each reporting verb to its grammatical pattern
Choose between verb + gerund, infinitive and that-clause
Report a passage mixing dialogue and narrative
Capture the exact function of each utterance

intro.en: Basic narration uses 'said' and 'asked'; advanced reported speech uses precise reporting verbs — admit, deny, suggest, warn, promise, refuse, threaten — each carrying the speaker's intention. The challenge is that these verbs follow different patterns (some take a gerund, some an infinitive, some a that-clause). Mastering them lets you report not just the words, but the meaning.
intro.hi: साधारण narration 'said' और 'asked' का प्रयोग करता है; उन्नत reported speech सटीक reporting verbs प्रयोग करता है — admit, deny, suggest, warn, promise, refuse, threaten — हर एक वक्ता की मंशा बताती है। चुनौती यह है कि ये क्रियाएँ अलग-अलग pattern लेती हैं (कुछ gerund, कुछ infinitive, कुछ that-clause)। इन्हें साधने से आप केवल शब्द नहीं, बल्कि अर्थ भी report कर पाते हैं।

real_life.situation:
Same fact, two reporting verbs:

Plain: He said that he had not taken the money.
Precise: He denied taking the money.
real_life.why: 'denied' captures his intention in one word and triggers a gerund ('taking'). Choosing the exact reporting verb makes the report shorter and more meaningful — the mark of a skilled writer and a high-scoring answer.

rule_box.html:
PatternReporting verbsExample
verb + gerundadmit, deny, suggest, recommenddenied taking it
verb + to-infinitivepromise, refuse, offer, agree, threatenrefused to go
verb + object + to-infadvise, warn, remind, urge, orderwarned me not to go
verb + that-clauseadmit, suggest, insist, complaininsisted that he was right
rule_box.formula: Pick the precise verb → use its correct pattern
rule_box.example: "I'll definitely help," he said. → He promised to help.

words.meaning: a verb naming a speech act

quick_test.q: Which reporting verb is followed by a gerund?

common_mistakes.wrong: He denied to take the money.
common_mistakes.note: 'deny' takes a gerund, not an infinitive.
'advise' needs an object before the infinitive.

fill_l1.instructions: Choose the correct form after each reporting verb.

fill_l2.instructions: Report each sentence with a precise reporting verb.

items.q: "You'd better not go out," mother told me.
items.answer: Mother advised/warned me not to go out.

items.q: "Yes, I made a mistake," he said.

error_detection.sentence: He admitted to steal the bag.
He advised to consult a lawyer. (no object)
error_detection.correct: He advised me to consult a lawyer.

sentence_correction.wrong: She suggested to go to the cinema.
sentence_correction.correct: She suggested going to the cinema. (or: She suggested that we go…)

sentence_correction.wrong: The captain ordered the men retreat.
sentence_correction.correct: The captain ordered the men to retreat.

rearrangement.jumbled: warned / not / he / to / me / go
rearrangement.answer: He warned me not to go.

reading.passage: "I'm afraid I broke your vase," Sam admitted. "I'm so sorry." His friend, however, refused to be angry. "Don't worry about it," he insisted. Sam promised to replace it and offered to pay at once. "You really mustn't," his friend warned him gently, suggesting instead that they simply forget the whole thing.

questions.q: Report 'I'm afraid I broke your vase' using a precise verb.
Which verb reports the friend's refusal, and what pattern does it take?
questions.answer: 'refused' — followed by a to-infinitive ('refused to be angry').

questions.q: Report the last utterance using 'suggest'.
questions.answer: He suggested forgetting the whole thing / suggested that they (should) forget it.

speaking: She promised to return the book.
They warned us not to swim there.
He refused to answer the question.

writing.prompt: Write a 4-line dialogue in direct speech (a confession, a promise, a piece of advice, a refusal), then report it using precise verbs (admit, promise, advise, refuse) with their correct patterns.
writing.example: Direct: "I forgot, sorry." "I'll do it tomorrow." / Reported: He admitted forgetting and promised to do it the next day.

options: She warned me not to go.
She warned me to not going.

challenge.q: Report precisely: '"It was me. I admit it," he said.'
Report: '"If you do that again, I'll call the police," he said.'
options: He threatened to call the police.
He threatened me call the police.

challenge.q: Report: '"Well done on passing the exam!" she said to him.'
options: She congratulated him on passing the exam.
She congratulated that he passed on.
